newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER SHOWCASE-ZOLA AIMS TO REPEAT HIS WEMBLEY HEROICS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-ZOLA AIMS TO REPEAT HIS WEMBLEY HEROICS.

text.p: Italian international Gianfranco Zola, who scored the winning goal for his country against England the last time he played at Wembley, says he owes it to Chelsea to the same for them at the Cup final on Saturday.
The diminutive striker said on Thursday the World Cup qualifier last February with its electric atmosphere "is fixed in my mind"
"I am very happy with Chelsea -- the club and the fans and I would like to give them the same satisfaction," he said at the club's training ground near London's Heathrow Airport.
Zola, dubbed "happy feet" by his captain Dennis Wise because of his supreme skill on the ball, said he was not allowing himself to feel any pressure before the final against Middlesbrough

"I know it's a special game. I know the supporters expect me to play a good game, but I also know I must stay normal and keep confident," the Sardinian, who joined Chelsea from Parma last November for 4.5 million pounds ($7.4 million), said.
Zola, accompanied by his father Ignazio on his first trip to England, will be presented with the county's Footballer of the Year award at a ceremony later on Thursday.
Chelsea are runaway favourites to win the Cup that has eluded them for 27 years, against Middlesbrough, who are having to contend with the disappointment of relegation.

But, despite the pressure of the occasion, players and manager Ruud Gullit said they were relaxed and confident. There was no sign of nerves as they joked and chatted with press and television at a news conference.
Gullit, veteran of several finals both with the Dutch national side and AC Milan, said with his customary cool that it was no use worrying.
"When I played my first final against Steaua Bucharest (for AC Milan in the European Cup) we were favourites and we just got on and did the job," he said.
"If you are confident about yourself and know where your strengths are you don't have to worry about anything."
But the 34-year-old player-manager said he was not looking upon Middlesbrough as a walkover.
"I am not approaching them as a relegation team but as a top team because they did not deserve to go down and they have good players," he said. "I don't fear them but I respect them."
Gullit said he had 21 players fit for the match. That would be whittled down to 18 on Friday and 16 would go to Wembley. The players would know who was in the side only on Saturday morning.

Gianluca Vialli, the Italian former international condemned mostly to the bench this season because of the successful attacking partnership of Zola and Mark Hughes, said he was resigned to playing second fiddle again on Saturday.
"I'd prefer to start, I'd prefer to be part of the team. But everyone is involved -- 11 on the pitch, three on the bench, the coach, all those in the back room.
"We have to do our best for the club and forget our own problems."
